## Problem

The pre-push hook pushes the checkpoint branch only to `origin` (`internal/hooks/prepush.go:32`, `git.PushBranch("origin", git.CheckpointBranch)`), whatever remote the user pushes to. Users with more than one remote (a fork and `upstream`, or a backup remote) do not get their checkpoints on the remote they push to, and a repository with no remote named `origin` gets a failed checkpoint push on each `git push`.

Git passes the remote name and URL to the pre-push hook as `$1` and `$2`. The installed hook scripts forward them (`partio _hook %s "$@"`, `internal/git/hooks/hooks.go:17` and `:32`), so `runHook` receives them after the hook name (`cmd/partio/hook.go:23`), but `prepush.go` does not use them.

## Proposed Solution

1. Push the checkpoint branch to the remote that git passes to the pre-push hook, instead of `origin`.
2. Add a `checkpoint_remotes` config option that takes a list of remote names.
3. When it is set, push the checkpoint branch to each listed remote during pre-push; a failure on one remote does not stop the others, and no failure fails the user's push.

Checkpoint reads stay local: `checkpoint.Read` and `FindByBranch` read the local `partio/checkpoints/v1` branch and fetch nothing (argos review, 2026-10-10), so no read change is needed.

Design point (from #532, closed): once checkpoints follow the pushed remote, a push to a fork or to a remote of another owner also gets the checkpoint branch. When `checkpoint_remotes` is set, push checkpoints only to the listed remotes, whatever remote the user pushes to.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The checkpoint push goes to the remote name that git passes to the pre-push hook
- [ ] A repository with no `origin` remote gets the checkpoint push on its other remote
- [ ] A config option `checkpoint_remotes` takes a list of remote names to push checkpoints to
- [ ] When more than one remote is set, the checkpoint branch is pushed to each of them during pre-push
- [ ] When `checkpoint_remotes` is set, a push to an unlisted remote does not push the checkpoint branch there
- [ ] A failed push to one remote does not stop the others or fail the user's push

Inspired by entireio/cli#1634 and #1635 (checkpoint reads hardcode origin; push queue drained by first push)
